entries.subject: node-headers-timeout-trap
entries.citationName: Node headersTimeout trap: smaller of keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout

deferredTo.reason: Attempted in B13 (2026-11-12): cannot run on this host. Node 10, 12 and 13 have no arm64 macOS build, and this host has no x64 runtime: Rosetta 2 is absent (`arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true` fails with "Bad CPU type in executable"; record: measure/results/2026-11-12-b13-attempt.txt). The trap was not measured; it needs Rosetta 2 or an x64 host.

entries.notes: Value 40 s is the default headersTimeout on 10.x (doc/api/http.md at v10.15.3 and v10.24.1, docs/research.md section 6). From the CVE-2019-5737 change until nodejs/node PR #32329 (12.19.0 and 13.13.0, never backported to 10.x) the headers timer also ran across the idle gap between keep-alive requests, so the idle close of an explicit keepAliveTimeout K is the smaller of K and headersTimeout. From the changelogs (CHANGELOG_V10, V12, V13) and the issue thread; not measured (docs/research.md sections 6 and 12). The extra second that later releases add to the idle close (see the Node 20.x and 22.x entries) was not measured on these releases and is not added. The research also lists 6.17.0, 8.15.1 and 11.10.1 as starts of the trap, but cites no default headersTimeout for 6.x, 8.x or 11.x, so those lines have no entry and are UNRESOLVED.
